memo.verdict: Neutral; park at EUR 57.3; medium conviction at the Triaging stage. The park is on the return alone: no D or F sits on management (RA 3, E 1, BB 4 at B), business quality (E 2, BB 2 at B), predictability (RA 8, E 2, BB 4 at B) or trackability (RA 7, E 2, BB 4 at B), so the gate rule does not fire. Two things re-open the case: the price near EUR 50 with the estimates intact (the modal path then clears 20 percent a year); or Labrie's margin and the cash conversion both clearing on the 2026-10-23 and February 2027 prints at a price near today's (the cleared branch gives 17 percent a year, a C, and with the upgrades a floor-setter tends to deliver, a B). Progress to Early-Stage only on one of those. The record's own summary: the business story is compelling; the investment at this price is not.
case: - The change is internal and multi-dimensional and already acting. Standalone since April 2025 (Kalmar demerged 2024; MacGregor sold 31 July 2025 for about EUR 220 million); Labrie bought 1 July 2026 with borrowed money, adding about a quarter to sales and a third to operating profit; a EUR 20 million cost programme (about 480 roles; the ZEPRO move from Bispgården to Stargard by end-2026; one-off cost about EUR 30 million, EUR 18 million booked); six divisions to three business areas on 1 April 2026 plus a fourth for Labrie; R&D to double by 2028; the 2026 margin floor raised three times. Of twelve screened internal forces one is A and nine are B; no screen red flag is present. The chief executive is not new: Scott Phillips has run Hiab since October 2018.

- The external cycle has turned from a two-year decline, but it is a recovery, not an inflection. Orders at a four-year high; Class 8 truck orders plus 8 percent in early 2026 with a six-to-twelve-month lag to crane bookings; Europe recovering since late 2024; the US delivery-equipment market at a trough, stabilising. Visibility about twelve months, not the two-plus years 'Demand Inflection' needs. Tariffs (US steel tariffs broadened to finished products August 2025; 25 percent on Mexican-built trucks; 40 percent of US-sold product imported from Europe; Labrie's Mexican maquiladora), rates and the dollar net the external forces to neutral (External forces C; Political and regulatory D).

- 'Financial Outputs' have followed as far as the estimates. Consensus 2027 EPS up 30 percent in six months; Services margin a record 26.1 percent against 23.7 percent consensus; margin rising from 13.4 percent to 14.9, 16.1, 16.3 percent on consensus; revenue growth minus 5.7 percent (FY2025) to plus 16.9, plus 19.7, plus 6.3 percent, about 26 points of the 2026-27 step acquired, organic about 0 to 2 percent in 2026 and about 5 percent in 2027. Upgrades likely but modest (floors are set to be beaten: 2024 above 12 to above 14 to 14.9 percent; 2025 above 12 to above 13.5 to 13.7 percent); the one-month revision is zero. Goldilocks growth B: about 28 percent a year over eighteen months to FY2027 EPS of EUR 3.85 (the record's path), 21 percent a year to FY2028 EPS of EUR 4.15, 14 percent a year from FY2026 to FY2029 (EUR 4.55). Cash conversion D: the H1 2026 shortfall has a stated cause (finished-goods inventory for H2 shipments, receivables timing) and is a forecast recovery, not a print.
counter_case: The strongest case against, at full force: Hiab is a company that sets floors it knows it will beat, and its beats are margin arithmetic over a shrinking commercial market. Q2 2026's order strength was one EUR 37 million key account, defence at 6 percent of orders and buying pulled forward ahead of tariffs, over Equipment organic sales still down 3 percent; this is the risks report's 'false friend' profile, a recovery that is not one, and its competing-hypotheses matrix found it the only profile with zero hard inconsistencies, against four for the bull and five for the bear. Management bought Labrie at a private-equity margin peak (EBITDA margin 21.8 percent from 15.1 percent in the year before Wynnchurch sold) with EUR 900 million of debt that took a net-cash company to about 70 percent gearing against a target below 50 percent, while operative cash flow fell to EUR 100 million from EUR 183 million for reasons revenue and margin do not explain and that management under-communicated. Labrie's return on the price paid is about 8 percent pre-tax, roughly 6 percent after tax before synergies, a third of the historical ROCE; integration and transaction costs (EUR 15 million) and PPA (EUR 23 million) land in H2 2026; its front and rear loaders come out of a Mexican maquiladora under a trade regime that can change. The surcharge model has made a truck-and-crane package dearer in a market where small buyers are already sweating assets; the dollar (54 percent of combined sales, EUR 8 million of EBIT per 10 percent after hedges) and tariffs cluster on one timeline with the integration; the injury rate doubled in the restructuring quarter; experts say Hiab is consistently dearer than Palfinger without superior reliability, Palfinger is easier to use and has recently out-executed Hiab, and Palfinger is spending EUR 50 million to take US service and crane share; tariffs can break down the duopoly's pricing power. The outcome: 2027 margins stagnate at 15.7 percent (the sell-side's own bear, EUR 50, minus 13 percent) or compress to 14.1 percent on 8.6x EV to adjusted EBITA (the risks report's bear, EUR 35, minus 39 percent). On the sorting, the case is a cyclical recovery with an acquisition bolted on: the 'major EPS trajectory upgrade' was bought, not produced, and the only box the organic business fits is the one it fails.

The record concedes every fact in it: the cash print is real and under-explained; the leverage is real and above target; Labrie's margin history is what it is; the Americas order growth was one order; the injury rate doubled; the EPS-trajectory upgrade is three-quarters acquisition arithmetic; the US service position is the one asset a funded rival can erode. The record's response: the Services margin of 26.1 percent on EUR 123 million is pricing power in the installed base, not a false friend; book-to-bill was above one in every region for two quarters and Equipment orders rose 21 percent, which one account does not do; the CFO attributed the guidance raise to continuing operations; the surcharge model has held the profit-and-loss account for eighteen months; industry prices did not fall through two years of falling volume and the gross margin rose 3.1 points; Palfinger's weakness (7.2 percent margin, targets pushed out) is relative support, not a sector collapse; the two things the bear needs, Labrie's margin and the cash, are dated tests with named thresholds. What the bear does to the rating: nothing, because the modal return is already a D at the modal multiple; the bear is why the uncleared branch is 12.0x and why the mark-to-market attribute is D, and the bear does not need to be right for the recommendation to be neutral.
triggers: - Labrie delivery (Key Driver, both tests): modal case a 17 percent comparable operating margin held through the first four consolidated quarters (Q3 2026 to Q2 2027) with service share rising from 10 percent; guidance 'about 17 percent' for H2 2026; Alarm: Labrie EBITDA margin below 20 percent in any quarter; Invalidate: below 18 percent for two quarters; to be inferred from the Equipment segment margin and commentary because Labrie is not reported on its own line from Q3 2026.

- US delivery-equipment cycle (Key Driver, both tests): modal case Americas orders up in Q3 and Q4 2026 without a single large account; Alarm: Class 8 orders down three consecutive months; Invalidate: US order intake not inflecting by Q1 2027.

- Cash conversion and deleveraging (Key Driver, both tests): modal case H2 2026 operative cash flow above EUR 150 million and gearing below 50 percent by end-2027 (about 47 percent on the record's calculation); Alarm: H2 2026 operative cash flow below EBIT; Invalidate: H1 2027 operative cash flow below EUR 150 million, or net debt to EBITDA above 2.5 times at end-2027.
- US trade policy (Key Risk, both tests): Alarm: a new tariff step on finished cranes or Mexican-built bodies; Invalidate: comparable margin below the prior floor of 13.5 percent for two quarters.
- Acquired margin bought at a peak (Key Risk): Alarm: Labrie backlog down two quarters; Invalidate as Labrie delivery.
- The multiple (Key Risk, share price): Alarm: below 12x with estimates unchanged; no Invalidate (a price, not a case fact); even odds of 15x once the two conditions clear.
